derivability_classes.definition: O_i ⊨ G_j AND Σ(A) = T_j for all admissible sets A containing T_j
O_i ⊨ G_j BUT Σ(A) does not guarantee T_j over alternatives
(O_i ∧ S_k) ⊨ G_j for additional state condition S_k beyond T_i's direct output

implication_chain: T5 output (spec): claim.status ∈ {'contradicted', 'disputed'} (disjunction)
T1 intrinsic: claim.status == 'contradicted' (specific element required)
Implication O_T5 ⊨ G_T1 fails: 'disputed' branch does not satisfy T1 intrinsic
Additional condition S_k1 required: T5 contradiction-check returned True (→ status='contradicted')
With S_k1: (O_T5 ∧ S_k1) ⊨ G_T1 — T1 intrinsic satisfied
Selection S_k2 required: original claim P is selected as focus in next iteration

select_focus_claim returns regular[0] (insertion-order in state.claims dict); P precedes counter-claim CC (CC was just created), but earlier-inserted unsealed claims may preempt P in multi-claim graphs
With S_k1 ∧ S_k2: select_operation(P) → status=='contradicted' at line 997 → T1 selected; no preemption possible (T1 is first non-bypass check)
required_state_conditions: S_k1: check_for_contradiction returned True (i.e., claim.status='contradicted', not 'disputed')
S_k2: original claim P is regular[0] in select_focus_claim (insertion-order and graph-topology dependent)
spec_side.selection_consideration: T1 is highest-priority non-bypass operator in select_operation. Once P is selected as focus and status='contradicted', T1 fires without preemption. The weak link is focus selection (S_k2), not operator selection.

implication_chain: T5 code (lines 780-843): calls _llm_json for counter-generation; creates C-prefixed counter with parent_id=claim.id; calls check_for_contradiction(claim, counter)
check_for_contradiction (lines 404-435): Path A (LLM): bool(result.get('contradicts', False)) — LLM-dependent, non-deterministic
check_for_contradiction Path B (LLM fails, Fallback 1): checks counter_predicate for neg_markers = ('not','never','no ','cannot',"can't",'doesn't','does not') — deterministic given counter content
check_for_contradiction Path C (LLM fails, Fallback 2): checks _OPPOSING_PAIRS across predicate+object fields — content-dependent

T5 double-fallback sub-path: if T5 LLM fails → counter_predicate = 'does not ' + claim.predicate (line 810); if check_for_contradiction LLM also fails → Fallback 1 fires; 'does not' IS in neg_markers → returns True → status='contradicted' DETERMINISTICALLY
General path: S_k1 required (check_for_contradiction LLM result is non-deterministic)
After T5: P (original, status∈{'contradicted','disputed'}) and CC (counter, status='unknown') are both unsealed, non-weak, branch_open=False → both in regular pool
select_focus_claim (lines 1063-1071): iterates state.claims in insertion order; P was inserted before CC; in single-claim graph P is regular[0]; in multi-claim graph earlier claims may preempt
S_k2 required: P is regular[0]; if CC or another claim is selected first, T3 fires on CC (evidence_refs=[], modality='hypothesis') — not T1
With S_k1 ∧ S_k2: select_operation(P) at line 997 → T1 fires
required_state_conditions: S_k1: check_for_contradiction returns True (LLM-dependent in general; guaranteed in double-LLM-failure sub-path where counter_predicate='does not '+claim.predicate and Fallback 1 fires)
S_k2: P (original claim) is selected as focus in next iteration (insertion-order + graph-topology dependent)
code_side.partial_determinism_finding: In the double-LLM-failure sub-path (T5 counter-generation LLM fails AND check_for_contradiction LLM fails), status='contradicted' is guaranteed: counter_predicate='does not '+claim.predicate contains 'does not' which is in neg_markers. In this sub-path, S_k1 is satisfied deterministically. The cascade becomes guard-derived for S_k2 in this sub-path.
code_side.selection_consideration: Focus selection after T5 is insertion-order dependent (regular[0] in state.claims). P precedes CC structurally, but multi-claim graphs may interpose other claims. If CC is selected first, T3 fires on CC, delaying the T5→T1 cascade. No priority mechanism favors P over other regular claims (unlike T9-ready priority for T3→T9).

cascades.rationale: Both spec-side and code-side classify T5→T1 as state-dependent with the same S_k structure (contradiction check → True; original claim focus-selected). Code analysis adds: (1) check_for_contradiction is confirmed LLM-dependent with heuristic fallbacks; (2) a deterministic sub-path exists (double-LLM-failure) where S_k1 is guaranteed. Neither predicate set produces strict or guard-derived classification.

implication_chain: T7 output (spec-side only): claim.qualifier != {} (confidence boost is '(per code)' and excluded)
T8 intrinsic: claim.status == 'supported'
T8 admissibility: claim.confidence > 0.8
T7 spec output does NOT imply T8 intrinsic: T7 does not set status
T7 spec output does NOT imply T8 admissibility: T7 spec has no confidence effect
Implication O_T7_spec ⊨ G_T8 fails on both components
Required: S_k1 = claim.status == 'supported' (pre-existing); S_k2 = claim.confidence > 0.8 (pre-existing — no spec-side T7 confidence effect)
Key observation: if S_k1 ∧ S_k2 hold before T7, T8_primary (line 1012) would fire on the same iteration IF T7 (line 1010) did not preempt it in the priority chain
T7 fires at line 1010 before T8_primary at line 1012 → T7 preempts T8 on the iteration when T7's intrinsic holds
After T7: qualifier != {} → T7 intrinsic no longer holds; on next iteration T8_primary fires if S_k1 ∧ S_k2 still hold (T7 spec does not change status or confidence, so they do)
Mechanism: T7 'clears itself' by setting qualifier; T8 fires next because T8's guard was already satisfied before T7. T7's spec output (qualifier != {}) is causally irrelevant to T8's admissibility.
With S_k1 ∧ S_k2: on next iteration, T6_primary skips (status='supported'), T7 skips (qualifier set), T8_primary fires
required_state_conditions: S_k1: claim.status == 'supported' before T7 fires (not produced by T7 spec output)
S_k2: claim.confidence > 0.8 before T7 fires (not produced by T7 spec output — spec has no confidence effect for T7)
Note: (S_k1 ∧ S_k2) ⊨ G_T8 independently; O_T7_spec contributes trivially (qualifier != {} plays no role in T8's guard)
spec_side.selection_consideration: After T7, same claim remains in graph (no new claim created). On next iteration, if the claim is selected as focus (insertion-order dependent): T6_primary skips (status='supported'), T7 skips (qualifier set), T8_primary fires at line 1012. No preemption. Selection deterministic given claim is focused.

implication_chain: T7 output (code): claim.qualifier != {} AND claim.confidence = min(1.0, claim.confidence + 0.05) (line 893)
T8 intrinsic: claim.status == 'supported'
T8 admissibility: claim.confidence > 0.8
T7 code output: qualifier != {} — does not imply T8 intrinsic (status unchanged)
T7 code output: confidence += 0.05 — participates in T8 admissibility if input confidence is in the right range
Narrow channel condition S_k2: 0.75 < confidence_pre_T7 ≤ 0.80
Lower bound (>0.75): ensures confidence_post_T7 = confidence_pre_T7 + 0.05 > 0.80 (satisfying T8 strict admissibility)
Upper bound (≤0.80): ensures T8_primary did NOT preempt T7 on previous iteration (T8_primary requires confidence > 0.8 strict; if confidence was ≤ 0.80, T8 didn't fire, T7 fired instead)
Verify T7 fired (not T6_primary): T6_primary requires status != 'supported'; with S_k1 (status='supported'), T6_primary skips; T7 fires at line 1010
After T7: confidence_post ∈ (0.80, 0.85]; status='supported' (S_k1); qualifier != {}
(O_T7_code ∧ S_k1 ∧ S_k2) ⊨ G_T8: status='supported' from S_k1; confidence > 0.8 from O_T7_code + S_k2
T7's confidence boost IS the enabling predicate that crosses T8's threshold in the narrow channel
required_state_conditions: S_k1: claim.status == 'supported' before T7 fires (not produced by T7)
S_k2: 0.75 < claim.confidence_pre_T7 ≤ 0.80 (narrow channel: T8 did not preempt T7, and T7's boost crosses T8's threshold)
code_side.selection_consideration: After T7 in narrow channel, same claim is in focus. On next iteration: T1-T5 skip (not contradicted, no conflict, has evidence, not underspecified, confidence > 0.4). T6_primary: status='supported' → skip. T7: qualifier set → skip. T8_primary: status='supported' AND confidence > 0.8 → fires. No preemption given S_k1 holds. Selection deterministic given claim focus.
code_side.key_difference_from_spec: Code-side T7 output (confidence += 0.05) participates in satisfying T8 admissibility; spec-side T7 output (qualifier != {} only) does not. The narrow channel (0.75, 0.80] is a code-side phenomenon; spec-side requires confidence > 0.8 as a pre-existing condition.

cascades.rationale: Both sides are state-dependent, but for different reasons. Spec-side: T7's output is causally irrelevant to T8's admissibility; the cascade is a priority-chain artifact where T7 fires before T8, clears itself, then T8's pre-existing guard fires. Code-side: T7's confidence boost (+0.05) is the enabling predicate in the narrow channel (0.75, 0.80]. The divergence corresponds to the spec_silent classification of T7's confidence boost in spec_code_discrepancy_matrix_v0-1.md.

implication_chain: T3 output (spec-side only): |claim.evidence_refs| >= 1 (I2 fallback predicates are '(per I2 fallback)' and excluded from spec-side)
T9 intrinsic is evaluated on PARENT claim P, not on T3's target branch B_j
T9 intrinsic: P.branch_open == True AND |branches(P)| > 0 AND all c in branches(P): c.status == 'supported'
T3 spec output (evidence_refs >= 1) does not address B_j.status
Spec has no mechanism by which T3 produces status='supported' on B-prefixed branch claims (I2 fallback is undocumented_extension, absent from spec)
Implication O_T3_spec ⊨ G_T9 fails: evidence_refs growth does not imply 'all branches supported'
Required S_k: S_k1 = P.branch_open==True; S_k2 = B_j.parent_id==P.id; S_k3 = B_j.status=='supported' (not from T3 spec); S_k4 = all other branches of P have status=='supported'
With S_k1 ∧ S_k2 ∧ S_k3 ∧ S_k4: G_T9 is satisfied on P
But S_k3 (B_j.status=='supported') is not derivable from T3 spec output — must come from an unspecified other source
T3's spec output (evidence_refs >= 1) participates trivially; the cascade has no spec-side mechanism
required_state_conditions: S_k1: P.branch_open == True (set by T1 when branches were created)
S_k2: B_j.parent_id == P.id (B_j is a child of P)
S_k3: B_j.status == 'supported' (NOT derivable from T3 spec output; must come from other source)
S_k4: all other branches of P already have status == 'supported' (rest-graph condition)
spec_side.selection_consideration: Spec-side has no mechanism for T3 to produce status='supported' on B_j. The cascade is formally state-dependent but causally empty at the spec level: T3's output does not contribute to T9's admissibility.

implication_chain: T3 code output for B-prefixed claims (evaluate_branch_claim, lines 470-486):
If LLM succeeds: claim.status = result.get('status', 'supported') — may be 'supported'
If LLM fails (I2 fallback, lines 484-486): claim.status = 'supported', claim.confidence = 0.85 — guaranteed
Analysis uses I2 fallback as the clearest case: B_j.status = 'supported' is guaranteed
T9 intrinsic is on P: P.branch_open==True AND branches(P)!=[] AND all c in branches(P): c.status=='supported'
branches(P) = {c ∈ state.claims | c.parent_id == P.id} (prefix-agnostic per code OQ3; includes C-prefixed claims with parent_id=P.id if T5 ever fired on P)
After T3 on B_j: B_j.status = 'supported' (from O_T3_code)

Additional S_k required: S_k1 = P.branch_open==True; S_k2 = B_j.parent_id==P.id; S_k3 = all other branches of P already status=='supported'; S_k4 = no C-prefixed claim with parent_id==P.id has status!='supported'
With O_T3_code(I2) ∧ S_k1 ∧ S_k2 ∧ S_k3 ∧ S_k4: all branches of P are 'supported', G_T9 satisfied
T3's code output (status='supported') IS the enabling predicate for B_j's contribution — unlike spec-side
Focus-claim selection: select_focus_claim (lines 1063-1071) checks branch_open claims: if children exist AND all supported → t9_ready.append(claim)
If S_k3 holds and B_j is now 'supported': P enters t9_ready
select_focus_claim returns t9_ready[0] with EXPLICIT PRIORITY over all regular claims
P is selected as focus (guaranteed by T9-ready priority mechanism, stronger than insertion-order)
select_operation(P): line 1014-1016: branch_open==True AND all branches supported → T9 fires
T9 fires; P.status after T1 is 'disputed', not 'contradicted', not is_synthesis — no preemption by T1/T2/T8-bypass
required_state_conditions: S_k2: B_j.parent_id == P.id (B_j is a child of P)
S_k3: all other branches of P already have status == 'supported' (rest-graph condition; T3 on B_j is the LAST step, completing the 'all supported' condition)
S_k4: no interfering C-prefixed claims with parent_id==P.id (prefix-agnostic branch collection; edge case when T5 fires on P)
code_side.selection_consideration: T9-ready priority in select_focus_claim guarantees P is selected as focus once all branches are supported. This is structurally stronger than the insertion-order-based selection for T5→T1 and T7→T8. Once P is focused, T9 fires at line 1014 without preemption (P.status='disputed' means T1 and T2 skip; P is not is_synthesis so T8-bypass skips; T3-T7 skip for other reasons in typical graph state).

cascades.rationale: Code-side has a real cascade mechanism: T3's I2 fallback (status='supported') is the enabling predicate, and select_focus_claim's T9-ready priority guarantees selection. Spec-side has no mechanism: I2 fallback is an undocumented_extension absent from spec predicates; T3's spec output (evidence_refs >= 1) contributes nothing to T9's guard. The divergence corresponds to the undocumented_extension classification of T3's I2 fallback in spec_code_discrepancy_matrix_v0-1.md.

cross_cascade_observations.title: No cascade achieves strict-derived
cross_cascade_observations.observation: All three tested cascades are state-dependent. None satisfy strict-derived (O_i ⊨ G_j AND Σ guarantees T_j). Additional state conditions (S_k) are required in all three cases. The conditions are non-trivial: they involve LLM execution outcomes (T5→T1), input-confidence range constraints (T7→T8), and rest-graph completeness conditions (T3→T9). This is a baseline finding for the pre-registered cascade set.

cross_cascade_observations.title: Spec/code divergence maps one-to-one to discrepancy audit findings
cross_cascade_observations.observation: T7→T8 and T3→T9 show spec/code divergence in cascade mechanism. T7→T8 divergence corresponds to 'spec_silent' for T7's confidence boost (spec_code_discrepancy_matrix_v0-1.md, T7 mutations). T3→T9 divergence corresponds to 'undocumented_extension' for T3's I2 fallback (spec_code_discrepancy_matrix_v0-1.md, T3 mutations). The cascade derivability check is sensitive to the same predicate gaps identified in the discrepancy audit.

cross_cascade_observations.title: Selection guarantee strength varies by cascade
cross_cascade_observations.observation: T3→T9 has the strongest selection guarantee: select_focus_claim implements explicit T9-ready priority (lines 1073-1074), guaranteeing P is selected once all branches are supported. T7→T8 is intermediate: no new claim is created, same claim remains in graph, T8 fires deterministically given claim is focused (no preemption in that state). T5→T1 is weakest: focus selection is insertion-order dependent in the regular list; multi-claim graphs may interpose other claims, causing the counter-claim to be processed by T3 first.

cross_cascade_observations.title: Partial determinism in T5→T1 double-fallback sub-path
cross_cascade_observations.observation: When T5's counter-generation LLM fails, counter_predicate = 'does not ' + claim.predicate. When check_for_contradiction's LLM also fails, Fallback 1 fires and finds 'does not' in neg_markers → returns True → status='contradicted'. In this sub-path, S_k1 is satisfied deterministically. This code-side finding is not visible at spec level and is not reflected in the canonical predicates.

cross_cascade_observations.title: T9-ready priority as a structural cascade enabler
cross_cascade_observations.observation: The T9-ready priority in select_focus_claim (lines 1073-1074) is a selection-policy feature that makes T3→T9 more reliable than the other two cascades. This priority prevents parent claims from competing with their own branches in focus selection. It is a selection-policy (SP-1) design choice with cascade-enabling consequences not described in any spec text.

summary_table.key_Sk: S_k1: contradiction check → True (LLM-dependent); S_k2: original claim selected as focus (insertion-order)
summary_table.note: Double-LLM-failure sub-path guarantees status='contradicted' deterministically; focus selection is the weak link

summary_table.key_Sk: Spec: S_k = status='supported' AND confidence>0.8 (pre-existing; T7 spec output irrelevant). Code: S_k = status='supported' AND 0.75<confidence≤0.80 (narrow channel; T7 confidence boost is enabling predicate)
summary_table.note: Spec/code divergence: T7 confidence boost absent from spec; changes S_k structure and causal relevance of T7 output

summary_table.key_Sk: Spec: T3 spec output contributes nothing to T9 guard; cascade mechanism absent from spec. Code: S_k = parent branch_open + all other branches supported; T3 I2 fallback (status='supported') is enabling predicate; T9-ready priority guarantees selection
summary_table.note: Strongest selection guarantee of the three (T9-ready priority); spec/code divergence corresponds to I2 undocumented_extension
